body:
Split out of #324, which is now scoped to the Check-time backstop alone so that 0.56 can close the size-reduction loop. This half improves the detector over time and is not needed to close it.

## Why it is separable

The backstop (#324) makes a decision from a threshold. This issue is about whether that threshold is still the right one a hundred bundles later. Those are different jobs on different clocks: one runs every cycle, the other at Act cadence.

It is also **blocked on evidence that does not exist yet**. The whole point is retuning against accumulated outcomes, and the outcomes accumulate only once the estimator has been running. Shipping it beside the thing it is meant to measure would mean tuning against an empty corpus.

## What it is

**1. A sizing column in the Act index.** `act.py`'s index gains estimate-vs-outcome, so the correlation is visible at Act cadence rather than only when someone runs `size-calibrate` by hand. Act is where cross-cycle patterns are already reviewed; a detector that silently drifts is exactly the kind of thing that review exists to catch.

**2. A documented retuning procedure** for `[driver.sizing]` from a fresh `size-calibrate` run, so the weights and cutoffs are revisited against evidence instead of ossifying at whatever the first calibration produced.

**3. The `model_weight` question.** Before calibration the model signal necessarily carries most of the weight — it is the only one that reads meaning rather than counting fields. As the corpus grows the structural weights should be tuned against evidence and the model becomes corroboration. That makes `model_weight` a config value a human revisits at Act cadence, not a constant baked into the engine.

## Why this matters more than it looks

0.56 already demonstrated the failure mode this exists to prevent. The published figures moved **67% → 62% precision** mid-milestone, not because the corpus changed but because a parsing fix made the estimator measure the brief correctly — `issue_507` had been read as 10.0 KB instead of 20.4 KB. The estimator got more correct and the number fell, meaning the earlier figure was partly an artifact.

Nobody would have noticed if a review had not gone looking. A number that only moves when someone thinks to re-derive it by hand is a number that will be wrong for a long time before anyone finds out. That is the argument for putting it in the Act index.

Related and still open: **#355** — four of the five weighted features read the whole brief rather than the a-priori text. Measured as latent today (0 of 86 corpus bundles), but it is exactly the kind of leak this loop should surface automatically rather than by inspection.

## Corpus quality, carried over from #324

`scripts/size-calibrate` cannot attribute pre-replan churn: an iterate-to-Plan archives the brief, so a bundle that churned hard and was then re-planned contributes its *final* brief with a low round count — 12 of 83 bundles in the originally observed corpus. Mining the archived `iteration-v*/brief.md` files as their own data points would recover that history and probably strengthen every correlation this loop depends on. Worth doing before leaning hard on the retuning.

## Definition of done

- `act.py`'s index carries the sizing column; `pdca act index` shows estimate vs. outcome.
- A documented procedure for retuning `[driver.sizing]` from a fresh `size-calibrate` run.
- `model_weight` is a config value with its Act-cadence review noted, not a constant.
- Reported on the PR: whether mining `iteration-v*/brief.md` changes the correlations, or an explicit decision not to.

Depends on #324 (there must be a `size-signal.json` to correlate against).

title: Act calibration loop: keep the sizing thresholds honest as the corpus grows
